text:
Mia Chen: Quick heads-up — validation run for the int4+fp8 attention POC finished. Posting highlights and a couple puzzlers.

Mia Chen: Perf/quality snapshot (test corpus: bookcorpus-100k, batch sizes vary):
```
path                  | tokens/s | mem/seq | ppl delta
fp32-ref              |  1200    |  1.0x   | base
fp8-only              |  1680    |  0.7x   | +0.8%
int8-fused            |  1820    |  0.65x  | +1.4%
int4-fused (stitch)   |  2040    |  0.52x  | +2.9%
int4 + fp8-hybrid     |  1960    |  0.55x  | +1.9%
```

Mia Chen: Positive: int4 fused kernel gives biggest throughput win and memory save. Negative: small but consistent ppl regression ~2.9% on int4-fused. Not huge but noticeable on long-context samples.

Sanjay Patel: Did you pin down where the quality hit comes from? attention softmax precision? kv-cache rescaling?

Mia Chen: Good q. I ran ablation: if we force fp32 softmax (dequant only for matmul inputs) the ppl drop to +1.1%. If we keep everything int4 including softmax the +2.9% remains. So softmax precision is a big factor.

Omar Reyes: Interesting. Could be head-wise scale variance — per-head scales under int4 lose dynamic range, softmax exaggerates differences. Any per-head scale tracking in the fused path?

Mia Chen: Current fused path uses a single per-tensor scale for QKV to simplify kernels. The hybrid path that uses per-head scale in dequant halves the regression. So we should move to per-head scales for attention.

Kelly Wu: That has ABI implications — our kernel selector expects a single scale ptr today. Adding per-head scales changes the function signature. Thoughts on backward compatibility?

Taylor Rivera: Proposal: keep existing ABI but add an optional "quant_meta" pointer (opaque) that kernel can inspect. If null, fall back to current behavior. If non-null, it contains a small table: {type, bits, per_head_scale_ptr, zero_point_ptr, layout_flags}. Opaque thing is 16 bytes on x86, 32 on aarch64.

Mia Chen: I sketched a minimal struct in the harness:
```c
struct quant_meta_t {
  uint8_t type; // 0=int8,1=int4,2=fp8
  uint8_t bits;
  uint16_t flags;
  float* per_head_scale; // nullable
  int32_t* zero_point; // nullable, bias correction
};
```
Mia Chen: Kernels that don't understand it just see null pointers and behave historically. Works for per-head scales and zero-point corrections.

Sanjay Patel: That looks fine, but two concerns: 1) pointers across process boundaries in Private deployments (we sometimes pass descriptors). Make sure the struct can be serialized (use offsets) or prefer handles. 2) alignment and vectorized load strategy on arm for per-head arrays.

Omar Reyes: For (1) we should support both direct pointers and an index into a shared buffer. The selector can translate handles at runtime. For (2) we should require per-head arrays to be 16-byte aligned and pad to 32-byte stride to help SVE/AVX2 loads. Add a flag in flags field for stride.

Kelly Wu: On the fused dequant vs wrapper debate: do we want a fused kernel that computes dequant+matmul+softmax in one op, or a dequant pre-step followed by existing matmul and softmax? Pros/cons?

Mia Chen: Fused wins latency and reduces memory bandwidth. But fused softmax in low precision needs careful accumulation and sometimes a small fp32 scratch for stable exp-sum. The wrapper approach is easier for correctness but loses bandwidth savings.

Taylor Rivera: Maybe allow both: provide a fused path with a strict numeric contract (e.g., must produce softmax within X delta of fp32 for up to 2048 seq) and a fallback wrapper path for strict correctness. The selector can pick based on model config, SLOs, or flagged workloads.

CI Bot: perf/harness job 1845679900 completed — binary: kernel-v2-quantmeta, tests: unit+integration passed except: attention-stress-int4 (3/10 flaky). Logs: https://ci/internal/1845679900

Mia Chen: CI shows flakes on attention-stress-int4 — I reproduced locally: intermittent NaNs when seq_len>1024 and batch small. Root cause looks like exp overflow in int4 softmax when head scales vary a lot.

Sanjay Patel: Can clamp logits before exp using per-head max subtract in fused kernel. Use dtype accumulation in fp16/fp32 for the exp-sum. That should remove NaNs.

Omar Reyes: Another edge: kv-cache reuse between fp32-ref and int4-fused paths. If cached K/V are quantized differently (per-batch vs per-head) we must re-quantize on route change. That can cost us a lot.

Mia Chen: Right now selector does route-local caches. If we route a request from fp32 to int4 fallback we mark cache invalid and recompute. That's heavy. Option: store cached K/V in both canonical fp32 form plus a lazy quantized view. Storage overhead but reduces rerun.

Kelly Wu: Storage overhead okay if it's optional. Maybe use an LRU for quantized views and limit per-request size. Add a flag to the routing policy to prefer cache-compatible kernels.

Taylor Rivera: Action items summary: \n- Move to per-head scale support in quant_meta (Mia + Omar)\n- Define serialized quant_meta ABI (Sanjay + Kelly) for Private/VM boundaries\n- Implement fused-softmax stability: clamp + fp32 accumulation fallback (Mia + Taylor)\n- Add lazy quantized KV cache view and routing hint (Omar)

Mia Chen: I can own the per-head perf runs next week and push a prototype patch for the quant_meta struct. I'll ping @Sanjay Patel and @Omar Reyes for review.

Sanjay Patel: I'll draft the serialized ABI doc and a quick shim that translates handles to pointers for the selector.

Omar Reyes: I'll prototype the lazy quantized KV cache and measure the re-route penalty.

Kelly Wu: I'll update the kernel selector checklist to include "quant_meta capability" and add gating for fused vs wrapper.

Taylor Rivera: We'll meet Fri 11am to review perf results and decide default route in selector.

Mia Chen: Thanks folks — closing loop here. If anyone sees an obvious miss in the plan call it out. :thumbsup:
